chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, from al-Munakhkhal, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the knowledge of the knowledgeable one, so he said to me: “O Jābir, indeed in the Prophets and the Awṣiyāʾ there are five spirits: the Spirit of Holiness, the spirit of faith, the spirit of life, the spirit of strength, and the spirit of desire.”
So by the Spirit of Holiness, O Jābir, they came to know what is beneath the Throne down to what is beneath the soil.
Then he said: “O Jābir, these four are spirits that are affected by the two occurrences, except for the Spirit of Holiness, for it neither becomes diverted nor plays.”

key_terms.الثَّرَى: the moist earth or soil beneath the ground
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: the successors appointed after the Prophets
key_terms.الْحَدَثَانُ: changing occurrences or events that affect created states
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, indicating the highest created realm
key_terms.رُوحَ الْقُدُسِ: the Holy Spirit through which special knowledge is granted
key_terms.عِلْمِ الْعَالِمِ: the knowledge of the divinely knowledgeable one

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the knowledge of the Prophets and the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the special constitution of the Prophets and the Awṣiyāʾ, stating that they possess five spirits. It highlights that through the Spirit of Holiness they know realities from beneath the Throne to beneath the earth, and that unlike the other four spirits, the Spirit of Holiness is not affected by changing conditions.
